lines.text: Imagine you've lived this same night four times, and nobody else remembers.
At midnight, everything resets. Except your phone.
Then it buzzes. A text, from your own number.
Rule one, from the first loop. When the lights die, don't move a muscle.
Eleven fifty-nine. Across the street, the windows go dark. One by one.
Block by block. Coming toward you.
Your building. The ground floor goes black. Then two. Then three.
Six goes dark. Then your lamp.
Your phone lights up. The last light in the city.
Last loop, I froze. It found me anyway.
A, freeze, like the rule says.
Or B, trust yourself, and run for the roof.
Comment A or B. The most voted choice decides loop five.
